alex: quick async check-in re: API gateway / routing policies / auth / rate limits — what I did / blockers / today
alex: What I did: landed PR #4123 — route-priority header + updated route-matcher unit tests. Also added a small guard to avoid batching qmodels.
alex: Blockers: saw intermittent 429s on canary when thinburst hits. Token bucket looks like it empties faster than expected for weighted routes. unsure if recent batching change increased concurrency.
alex: Today: pairing with @kevin to tune ratepolicy and run a 10% canary smoke.
kevin: I pulled the canary logs — one suspicious metric: token_refill_ms seems off for routes with weight >1. added quick log extract:
kevin: ```json
{"route":"/v1/chat","tokens":0,"refill_ms":100}
```
kevin: I'll draft a tiny fix to ratecalc today (should be low-risk).
priya: I can repro locally and in staging — I have a thinburst harness. I'll run it at 11:30 PT and share results + flamegraph. also will validate auth KID rotation didn't drop Authorization header.
lia: deploy-bot: starting canary deploy to eu-west-1 :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary rollout 10% initiated by lia — build 2026.03.18-111
kevin: @alex heads-up: your branch needs a rebase — auth middleware change added an extra header check. small conflict.
alex: rebased & pushed; fixed conflict and added guard to skip quantized-model routes from batching.
priya: staging run finished — reproduced 429s with burst=3000rps; attaching gist: https://gist.redwood/fake/abc123 (results + p99 latency chart).
lia: plan: wait for kevin's ratecalc patch + verify priya's results. if green, expand canary to 30% and run full smoke suite.
lia: reminder: update runbook with new ratepolicy param `short_burst_threshold` if we change default.
kevin: ack — opening PR to adjust refill calc and adding unit tests. will include a note for runbook.
alex: no other blockers from me. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: ack, watching the canary and will roll forward if smoke passes.
_note: This file is a single Slack thread in the eng-platform channel: daily async check-in focused on gateway/routing/auth/rate limits. Messages are chronological and formatted with sender prefixes as required.
